---
title: "Dialysis facility density and early dialysis initiation: a replication"
format: html
---

## The study

Hemmige and colleagues studied 844,466 adults who started in-center hemodialysis in the United States from 2011 to 2019, using the US Renal Data System (USRDS) [@hemmige2024density]. Patients living in Health Service Areas (HSAs) with the most dialysis facilities per resident had higher odds of starting dialysis at an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) above 10 mL/min/1.73 m²: an odds ratio of 1.06 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.10) compared with HSAs with no facility. The [clinical background](quarto/background.qmd) page explains why that matters.

## What this site does

This repository reproduces the paper's analysis from public code. The original analysis was a single R Markdown file of more than 3,000 lines (shown [here](quarto/original.qmd), with local file locations removed). It is rebuilt with packages that do the repetitive work:

-   **usRds** [@usrds_pkg] loads and labels the USRDS files, and attaches CMS dialysis facility counts to each patient by the date dialysis started.
-   **flowchart** [@flowchart_pkg] applies every exclusion and counts it at the same time, so the cohort diagram is the cohort.
-   **tidycensus** [@tidycensus] downloads the American Community Survey, and every other area-level file is downloaded from its publisher.

Rebuilding the analysis this way turned up several errors in the original code. They are corrected here, and each one is listed, with what it can change, on the [differences page](quarto/differences.qmd). Where the original code and the paper disagree, the choice is left to the investigators.

## Methods

The authoritative specification is [`analysis-plan.md`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/analysis-plan.md). In brief: incident adults on in-center hemodialysis with an eGFR of 20 or below; exposure, HSA dialysis facilities per 100,000 residents in five categories; outcome, eGFR above 10 at initiation; mixed-effects logistic models with a random intercept for HSA, progressively adjusted for patient, clinical, area and HSA characteristics [@vonelm2007strobe; @benchimol2015record].

## Status

The code is complete and tested on synthetic data. It has not yet been run on the USRDS data, so this site shows code and methods only; no results from USRDS data are published here. Open decisions are tracked as [GitHub issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/issues).
